bull_bear.body: Priority 1: New store openings in cluster approach. Priority 2: Strategic inventory procurement to hedge against OEM price hikes/supply shocks. Priority 3: Balance sheet strengthening. No dividends or buybacks highlighted; reinvestment mode.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution risk in new states (UP/MP/Chhattisgarh) vs Bihar maturity; Supply chain disruptions (Gulf war impact on gas/components); Real estate rental inflation (though currently stable in target regions); Margin recovery dependency on normalizing summer demand for cooling category.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and resilient. Emphasizes transition to 'all-weather' business model. Defensive on specific margin data (state-wise/mature vs new) citing competition, but clear on strategic intent to prioritize market share over short-term margin spikes during price hikes.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Inventory buildup (INR 840cr) is a deliberate arbitrage play on anticipated OEM price hikes (8-10%) and supply constraints, not just demand buffering. The 'weak' FY26 actually accelerated the maturity curve by forcing reliance on non-summer quarters, proving the H2 growth engine.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet framed as conservative: 'Low debt balance sheet', 'Operates on a cash-and-carry model' and 'Efficient inventory management and high cash reserves'.
- Deleveraging shown on the FY22-FY26 charts: the 'Net Debt to EBITDA (x)' series reads 1.5, 1.4, 0.2, 0.7, 0.3 and 'Net Debt to Equity (x)' reads 1.6, 1.4, 0.1, 0.2, 0.1.
- Growth has been part-funded by equity: FY2024 saw the 'First fund raise after IPO from the one of the World's largest FII - Capital Group'.
- Receivables are structurally negligible - the deck notes 'Receivable Days are less than 0 since the Company has negligible Trade Receivables' - so working capital is inventory and payables driven.
- No dividend policy, buyback or payout commentary appears anywhere in the deck.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Over 50% market share in Bihar and the largest electronics retailer in Jharkhand, giving regional dominance in underpenetrated markets
- 207 stores averaging 4,400+ sq. ft. and ~9.1 lakh sq. ft. of retail footprint across four states, built through prudent cluster-led expansion
- Physical retail model acts as a moat in regions where direct brand interaction remains critical
- Strong vendor partnerships and direct relationships with 100+ leading OEM brands, of which 85% of supply is direct OEM; no private labels
- Customer centricity through in-store experience, after-sales service (Aditya Seva) and access to flexible financing options
- Cash-and-carry model with low debt, controlled inventory and high cash reserves
- CRISIL Ratings reaffirmed 'CRISIL A/Stable' on long-term bank facilities in February 2026, citing established market position and sound operating efficiency
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Regulatory risk — MD&A: the Company may face disruption in business operations in the event of non-compliance with new policies or changes in existing policies; it mitigates by monitoring policy changes, engaging policymakers and diversifying markets.
- Market / competitive intensity risk — MD&A: lucrative growth prospects of the industry lead to heightened competitive intensity from regional and national players; the Company relies on brand equity, product offering, service, reach and customer centricity as its edge.
- Seasonal demand risk — MD&A: seasonality causes fluctuations in consumer demand that may lead to inventory imbalances and revenue volatility; managed via demand forecasting and season-based promotions. FY26 demonstrated this — an extended monsoon and one of the weakest summers in decades weighed on cooling-led demand in Q1 FY26.
- Supply chain risk — MD&A: smooth supply chains are imperative for timely procurement at competitive prices; disruption may raise cost, cause delays and reduce profitability and brand equity. Mitigated through a network of channel partners (the disclosure is cut off mid-sentence in the report text supplied).
- Geographic and single-activity concentration — BRSR Section A: operations are in only four states (Bihar 118, Jharkhand 33, Uttar Pradesh 53, Chattisgarh 3 showrooms; 207 total), with retail trade of electronic products accounting for 98.06% of turnover and exports nil — leaving performance tied to Hindi Heartland consumption and, disproportionately, to Bihar.
- Commodity pricing, chip shortage and global supply disruption — MD&A industry overview: the consumer durables sector faces volatility in commodity pricing, an acute shortage of chips, and impact on both demand and supply from the ongoing Middle East crisis; GDP growth for FY27 is projected to decline to 6.9% with the Middle East conflict a key downside risk.
- Regulatory transition in energy-efficiency labelling — From January 01, 2026 the Bureau of Energy Efficiency updated star rating and labelling norms, raising efficiency standards and prompting companies to clear pre-update inventories — a mix and inventory risk for the retail channel.
- Employee attrition — BRSR: turnover rate for permanent employees was 15.50% in FY26 (12.55% male, 2.95% female), against 16.70% in FY25 and 17.45% in FY24, on a base of 2,861 permanent employees and no workers.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- Deck claims '50%+ Mkt Share' in Bihar 'as per Crisil Report' and 'Largest Electronic Retailer in Jharkhand', plus '1st Consumer Electronics Retailer To be listed' (BSE 2016, NSE 2024).
- 'Zero Store Closure since Inception' since the first Patna store in FY1999; 100% retail sales with no private labels, purely a multi-brand retailer of 100+ OEM brands.
- Frames its addressable base as the Hindi heartland: Bihar, Jharkhand, UP and Chhattisgarh together '~31% of India's Estimated Population' (deck's per-state figures: UP 24 Cr, Bihar 13 Cr, Jharkhand 4 Cr, Chhattisgarh 3 Cr).
- Positions physical stores as structurally advantaged for premium, high-ticket purchases - 'physical stores help enhancing the perception of a brand', 'high-touch customer experience', and 'Good after sale service plays a major role while buying a high-ticket item'.
- Rides an organised-sector shift: deck cites organised share of consumer durables retail moving from 49% (FY16) / 58% (FY21) to 77% (FY27P) per CRISIL Research.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demand environment] Q1 FY27 demand was weather-split: 'East remained 5-8 degrees C cooler than North/Central during most of April & May', with Bihar and Jharkhand seeing intermittent rain and softer demand while UP's sustained heat supported cooling demand.
- [Consumer sentiment] Deck argues 'Sentiment, not income, became the key constraint', citing public messaging on gold read as a cue to 'Spend Less, Save More', LPG cylinder availability concerns, and a Rs 1,000 petrol pump purchase limit that led households to preserve cash.
- [Governance] Board is promoter-heavy at the executive level (Chairman & MD Yashovardhan Sinha, two promoter whole-time directors, two promoter non-executive directors) against six independent directors including ex-Samsung India and ex-UCO Bank veterans.
- [Demographics] Deck notes India's fertility has fallen below replacement (TFR 1.9) while its target states remain above it - Bihar 2.9, Uttar Pradesh 2.6, Madhya Pradesh 2.4, Chhattisgarh 2.2, Jharkhand 2.1.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Incorporated in 1999 at Patna, the Company operates a brick-and-mortar, multi-brand retail chain selling televisions, air conditioners, refrigerators and washing machines, digital gadgets such as mobile phones and laptops, and personal care and kitchen appliances, to customers in urban centres and emerging Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets of the Hindi Heartland. As on March 31, 2026 it ran 207 stores with an average store size of 4,400+ sq. ft. and a retail footprint of ~9.1 lakh sq. ft. across Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh. Retail trade of electronic products contributes 98.06% of turnover; customers are B2B and B2C, exports are nil, and the Company is not engaged in any production or manufacturing activity.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Creeping cluster expansion — scale through focused, cluster-led store additions in underpenetrated Hindi Heartland markets; 32 stores added in FY26 and 102 stores in the last three years versus 105 stores built over the previous 24 years
- Geographic deepening then widening: after 100% district coverage in Bihar and near-total penetration in Jharkhand, extend across Eastern, Central and Western Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, with entry into Madhya Pradesh and West Bengal underway
- Stay offline-first — remain committed to brick-and-mortar retail while consistently matching pricing with leading e-commerce platforms, protecting both margins and the customer experience
- Direct OEM sourcing at scale: 85% direct OEM supply and 15% through distributors/C&F agents, long-term relationships with 100+ brands and no private labels, enabling competitive pricing and superior margins
- Customer-first proposition 'Sambandh Bharose Ka' — best range, lowest price, fastest installation and great after-sales service, supported by Aditya Seva, Aditya Suraksha and the Buy & Win loyalty programme
- Financial discipline: low-debt balance sheet, cash-and-carry model, efficient inventory management and high cash reserves
- Prudent capital allocation with strong corporate governance, and a people-centric culture within a technology-driven business, with ESOPs accessible to every employee regardless of position
- The Board has adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations which endeavours for fairness, consistency and sustainability while distributing profits to shareholders. For FY26 the Board recommended a final dividend of 125%, or ₹1.25 per equity share of ₹1 face value, placed before members at the 27th AGM on September 02, 2026. The Company accepted no fixed deposits during FY26; details of loans, guarantees and investments under Section 186 are left to the notes to the financial statements. Foreign exchange earnings and outgo were NIL in both March 31, 2026 and March 31, 2025.
- The Company states it has set NO specific ESG commitments, goals or targets with defined timelines (BRSR Section B, Q5: 'No'; Q6 performance against such targets: 'NA').
- ISO 9001:2015 is the only national/international code, certification, label or standard the Company reports as adopted and mapped to the NGRBC principles.
- The BRSR is prepared on a standalone basis; name of assurance provider and type of assurance obtained are both 'NA' — the report is unassured.
- No independent assessment or evaluation of the working of its policies by an external agency has been carried out for any of the nine principles.
- The Company reports it does NOT have an anti-corruption or anti-bribery policy (BRSR Principle 1, Q4: 'No'), and does NOT have procedures in place for sustainable sourcing (Principle 2: 'No').
- R&D and capex investments in technologies to improve the environmental and social impacts of products and processes were 0 in both the current and previous financial year.
- Extended Producer Responsibility is reported as not applicable to the entity's activities; processes to reclaim plastics, e-waste, hazardous and other waste are reported as 'NA', and no Life Cycle Assessment has been conducted.
- Material responsible business conduct issues identified are both opportunities rather than risks — 'Customer Engagement and Satisfaction' and 'Market Presence, distribution Network & Channels' — each with positive financial implications and no mitigation approach stated.
- Nil fines, penalties, punishment, settlement or compounding fees paid in proceedings with regulators, law enforcement agencies or judicial institutions in FY26, and zero disciplinary actions against Directors/KMPs/employees for bribery or corruption in FY26 and FY25.
- Customer complaints: 35 filed in FY26 (20 in FY25) with none pending at year-end; complaints from communities, shareholders and employees were nil in both years.
- No complaint on sexual harassment was received during FY26; the Company has a POSH policy and states compliance with the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961.
- Governance of sustainability sits with the Managing Director, Yashovardhan Sinha (DIN 01636599), as the highest authority for BR policy implementation and as the specified Board authority for sustainability decision-making; NGRBC performance and statutory compliance are reviewed quarterly by Committees of the Board.
- Diversity: women are 40% of the Board of Directors (4 of 10) and 40% of Key Management Personnel (2 of 5); 20 permanent employees are differently abled out of 2,861 permanent employees.
- Energy consumption is minimal and limited to offices and showrooms as the Company is not engaged in any production or manufacturing activities; foreign exchange earnings and outgo were NIL in FY26 and FY25.
- ESOPs are widely distributed and accessible to every employee regardless of position; 4,75,000 equity shares were allotted under the ESOP Plan 2021 during FY26.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Expansion for Aditya Vision is store roll-out, not plant capex. During FY26 the Company opened 32 new stores across four states — 6 in Bihar, 4 in Jharkhand, 19 in Uttar Pradesh and 3 in Chhattisgarh — crossing the milestone of 200 operational stores through focused, cluster-led expansion. As on March 31, 2026 the store count stands at 207: Bihar 118 (all 38 districts), Jharkhand 33 (22 of 24 districts), Uttar Pradesh 53 (30 of 75 districts) and Chhattisgarh 3 (2 of 33 districts); retail footprint rose 22% to 9,13,725 sq. ft. with an average store size of 4,400+ sq. ft. Under 'Strategic Growth Pillars and Future Outlook' the Company states it plans to add at least 25–30 stores annually over the next 2–3 years on the base of 207 stores, anchored in sustaining strong double-digit same-store sales growth. It is focused on deepening presence across Bihar, Jharkhand, Eastern, Central and Western Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, and on entering Madhya Pradesh and West Bengal in the current calendar year, targeting underpenetrated markets. Operations run on a cash-and-carry model with 100+ brand partnerships and real-time API integration enabling rapid replenishment; consumer-finance tie-ups include Bajaj Finserv, HDB Financial Services, IDFC First Bank, Paytm, Pine Labs, Samsung Finance+ and TVS Credit. The annual report states no rupee capex quantum for this expansion, and BRSR Principle 2 reports nil R&D and nil capex in technologies to improve environmental and social impacts in both the current and previous financial year.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Income infusion at the grassroots: ₹10,000 direct transfer to women in Bihar under Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana, ~1.30 crore beneficiaries and ₹13,000 Crore of liquidity injected, strengthening rural cash flows
- Structural household savings: free electricity up to 125 units/month in Bihar covering ~1.8 crore households under Mukhyamantri Vidyut Upbhokta Sahayata Yojana, worth ~₹900/month per household of recurring savings
- Pricing-led demand stimulus from GST 2.0 rationalization — tax reduction from 28% to 18% across key categories (ACs, dishwashers, TVs above 32 inches) and a ~7–8% reduction in retail prices
- Product-mix upgrade cycle from the BEE norm transition — shift toward 3-star and above appliances plus OEM discounting on outgoing inventory, driving replacement demand
- Credit-enabled consumption: strong growth in consumer financing and rising personal loan penetration across key markets
- Salary-led upside from the 8th Pay Commission, with a ~30–35% salary increase for government employees and pensioners lifting urban discretionary spending
- Diversified portfolio reduces seasonality — with summer categories soft in H1 FY26, washing machines, water purifiers and induction cooktops picked up, and H1 and H2 contributed almost evenly to annual performance
- Quarterly Y-O-Y growth accelerated through FY26 at 6%, 22%, 27% and 28%, delivering 18% topline growth despite the weakest summer in over two decades
- Industry backdrop: Indian consumer durables market valued at ₹6,240 Billion projected to grow at ~11% CAGR to ₹9,470 Billion by 2029, with shortening replacement cycles and service quality becoming a key retailer differentiator
- Watch-items flagged for the sector: commodity price volatility, an acute shortage of chips, and demand/supply impact from the ongoing Middle East crisis
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Aditya Vision successfully pivoted from a H1-heavy seasonal model to an all-weather performer, delivering 28% Q4 revenue growth despite a weak summer, driven by strategic inventory stocking ahead of OEM price hikes and accelerated expansion in Uttar Pradesh. The shift in product mix toward higher-ASP but lower-margin mobiles/laptops compressed reported margins, masking the underlying operating leverage maturing stores will provide in FY27.

open.item: Do not foresee raising any equity capital this financial year or near-term; internal accruals plus short-term working-capital borrowings sufficient for expansion and inventory.
Company plans to add more than 30 stores per year (guides conservatively at 25) via calibrated cluster expansion; will not give a firm number.
On track to enter Madhya Pradesh this financial year (FY27), having already entered Chhattisgarh with 3 stores earlier than planned; a neighbouring state also opening up for expansion.
Store expansion is anchored in sustaining strong double-digit Same-Store Sales Growth (SSSG).
The Company plans to add at least 25–30 stores annually over the next 2–3 years, building on a network of 207 stores as of March 31, 2026.
Strategy to make newer states (UP, Chhattisgarh, MP) gradually catch up to Bihar's mature-state margins over time without compromising sales.
The Company is focusing on scaling premium and sunrise categories to enhance per-store economics.
Stores get to breakeven between 9 and 12 months from opening (mature by ~3 years).
As ~50% of stores cross 3 years and fewer new stores are added in percentage terms, management expects better control over operating expenses and a margin lever near-term.
Management claims the business is now an all-weather, all-season company, with H2 becoming as important as H1 (previously Q1/Q2 were 55-60% of annual sales).
Endeavour to reach back toward 9% EBITDA margin; standing guidance range of 8% to 10%.
Company will not sell private-label products as per policy; sells only branded stock.
Reiterated long-term potential of around 500 stores across current states over a long horizon.
New store revenue model of ~Rs.6 crore in first year, Rs.12 crore in second, Rs.18 crore in third year is broadly holding, with many stores doing better than guided.

currentContext.expansion: Expansion for Aditya Vision is store roll-out, not plant capex. During FY26 the Company opened 32 new stores across four states — 6 in Bihar, 4 in Jharkhand, 19 in Uttar Pradesh and 3 in Chhattisgarh — crossing the milestone of 200 operational stores through focused, cluster-led expansion. As on March 31, 2026 the store count stands at 207: Bihar 118 (all 38 districts), Jharkhand 33 (22 of 24 districts), Uttar Pradesh 53 (30 of 75 districts) and Chhattisgarh 3 (2 of 33 districts); retail footprint rose 22% to 9,13,725 sq. ft. with an average store size of 4,400+ sq. ft. risks.note: MD&A: the Company may face disruption in business operations in the event of non-compliance with new policies or changes in existing policies; it mitigates by monitoring policy changes, engaging policymakers and diversifying markets.

MD&A: lucrative growth prospects of the industry lead to heightened competitive intensity from regional and national players; the Company relies on brand equity, product offering, service, reach and customer centricity as its edge.

MD&A: seasonality causes fluctuations in consumer demand that may lead to inventory imbalances and revenue volatility; managed via demand forecasting and season-based promotions. FY26 demonstrated this — an extended monsoon and one of the weakest summers in decades weighed on cooling-led demand in Q1 FY26.

MD&A: smooth supply chains are imperative for timely procurement at competitive prices; disruption may raise cost, cause delays and reduce profitability and brand equity. Mitigated through a network of channel partners (the disclosure is cut off mid-sentence in the report text supplied).

BRSR Section A: operations are in only four states (Bihar 118, Jharkhand 33, Uttar Pradesh 53, Chattisgarh 3 showrooms; 207 total), with retail trade of electronic products accounting for 98.06% of turnover and exports nil — leaving performance tied to Hindi Heartland consumption and, disproportionately, to Bihar.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers

- Pricing-led demand stimulus from GST 2.0 rationalization — tax reduction from 28% to 18% across key categories (ACs, dishwashers, TVs above 32 inches) and a ~7–8% reduction in retail prices
- Product-mix upgrade cycle from the BEE norm transition — shift toward 3-star and above appliances plus OEM discounting on outgoing inventory, driving replacement demand
- Credit-enabled consumption: strong growth in consumer financing and rising personal loan penetration across key markets
- Salary-led upside from the 8th Pay Commission, with a ~30–35% salary increase for government employees and pensioners lifting urban discretionary spending
- Diversified portfolio reduces seasonality — with summer categories soft in H1 FY26, washing machines, water purifiers and induction cooktops picked up, and H1 and H2 contributed almost evenly to annual performance
- Quarterly Y-O-Y growth accelerated through FY26 at 6%, 22%, 27% and 28%, delivering 18% topline growth despite the weakest summer in over two decades
- Industry backdrop: Indian consumer durables market valued at ₹6,240 Billion projected to grow at ~11% CAGR to ₹9,470 Billion by 2029, with shortening replacement cycles and service quality becoming a key retailer differentiator

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demand environment] Q1 FY27 demand was weather-split: 'East remained 5-8 degrees C cooler than North/Central during most of April & May', with Bihar and Jharkhand seeing intermittent rain and softer demand while UP's sustained heat supported cooling demand.
- [Consumer sentiment] Deck argues 'Sentiment, not income, became the key constraint', citing public messaging on gold read as a cue to 'Spend Less, Save More', LPG cylinder availability concerns, and a Rs 1,000 petrol pump purchase limit that led households to preserve cash.
- [Governance] Board is promoter-heavy at the executive level (Chairman & MD Yashovardhan Sinha, two promoter whole-time directors, two promoter non-executive directors) against six independent directors including ex-Samsung India and ex-UCO Bank veterans.
- [Demographics] Deck notes India's fertility has fallen below replacement (TFR 1.9) while its target states remain above it - Bihar 2.9, Uttar Pradesh 2.6, Madhya Pradesh 2.4, Chhattisgarh 2.2, Jharkhand 2.1.

margins & cost dynamics: Gross Margin: 16% (Q4), 15.6% (FY26). EBITDA Margin: 8.1% (Q4), 8.5% (FY26). Pressure from low-margin high-ASP mobile/laptop mix. Operating expenses rose due to expansion freight, credit card commissions, and brand ambassador fees. Management expects opex to stabilize as new store % declines relative to mature base.
capex / expansion: Funded via internal accruals and working capital borrowings. No equity dilution planned. Spend directed toward new store openings (30+ run-rate) and strategic inventory buildup (INR 840cr).
capital allocation: Priority 1: New store openings in cluster approach. Priority 2: Strategic inventory procurement to hedge against OEM price hikes/supply shocks. Priority 3: Balance sheet strengthening. No dividends or buybacks highlighted; reinvestment mode.
risks & watch-items: Execution risk in new states (UP/MP/Chhattisgarh) vs Bihar maturity; Supply chain disruptions (Gulf war impact on gas/components); Real estate rental inflation (though currently stable in target regions); Margin recovery dependency on normalizing summer demand for cooling category.
management quality / tone: Confident and resilient. Emphasizes transition to 'all-weather' business model. Defensive on specific margin data (state-wise/mature vs new) citing competition, but clear on strategic intent to prioritize market share over short-term margin spikes during price hikes.
non-obvious takeaways: Inventory buildup (INR 840cr) is a deliberate arbitrage play on anticipated OEM price hikes (8-10%) and supply constraints, not just demand buffering. The 'weak' FY26 actually accelerated the maturity curve by forcing reliance on non-summer quarters, proving the H2 growth engine.

| Supply chain constraints and raw material (gas) shortages leading to OEM price hikes | Voltas | beneficiary | Med | Aditya's strategic stocking indicates anticipated strong demand and price firmness in AC segment, benefiting manufacturers with pricing power. |

themes.title: Quick-commerce, omnichannel & retail expansion
themes.need: Quick-commerce and value retail are the structural growth engine, and Q1FY27 rewrote the unit-economics model. ETERNAL raised Blinkit's steady-state margin from a 5-6% range to ~6% and set a first-ever 4% GAAP EBIT margin target (after ESOP and depreciation) while capex per store went from INR 1cr to INR 2.5cr (+150%) with NOV/store/day up only 60% and net working capital improving 18 to 14 days - so margin can now drift DOWN while ROCE improves. Growth also decoupled from spend: Blinkit orders +21% QoQ with MTUs above 30mn achieved on LOWER marketing spend and fewer store adds, and management called Q1 the peak of competitive intensity to date. VMM did INR 3,727cr (+18.7%) on 10% SSSG with gross margin up to 28.7% driven by lower promotional spend rather than price hikes, validated a small-format store at the same revenue/sq ft and 'pretty much the same' ROCE as large format (a ~3,000-store national opportunity), and found 20% of its quick-commerce customers had never shopped a Vishal store. SHOPERSTOP swung PAT positive (+INR 5cr vs -INR 4cr) and raised FY27 LFL guidance from 5% to ~6%; ARVINDFASN lifted gross margin 90bps to 56.7% on full-price sell-through with direct channels now 62% of sales; MEESHO cut cost per delivered order ~INR 1 QoQ despite the May fuel hike. DMART/V2RETAIL/PATELRMART on value retail; TRENT-tier branded retail via ABFRL/METROBRAND/BATAINDIA/REDTAPE.
themes.driver: Blinkit dark-store rollout at the new INR 2.5cr/store capex against the 4% GAAP EBIT target; VMM small-format expansion; festive/quick-commerce GMV. Watch ARVINDFASN's SS27 sourcing lock (next 45-60 days) - if war-inflated input costs hold, apparel pricing corrects.

themes.title: Consumer durables, cooling & electricals
themes.need: Rising incomes, electrification and a record cooling season drive consumer-electricals and appliances - HAVELLS/VOLTAS/BLUESTARCO/SYMPHONY/ORIENTELEC on cooling & electricals; TTKPRESTIG/STOVEKRAFT/BAJAJELEC/EUREKAFORB on kitchen/home; CROMPTON-tier fans & pumps; premiumization + GST 2.0 + summer demand expand the organized share. Q1FY27's small-cap read: SONAMLTD grew revenue 75.6% YoY to INR 66.57cr on a cheap raw-material inventory position taken 6-7 months in advance while selling prices rose - management explicitly called the 75% print non-repeatable and guided FY27 to 25-30% with a Q2 floor of INR 40-50cr - and is pivoting from volume to INR 5,000-15,000 value clocks with capacity utilisation still only 60-70%.
themes.driver: Summer cooling demand; GST 2.0 price cuts; festive restocking; commodity-cost tailwind on margins; premiumization/ASP mix shift.

hero.oneLiner: Aditya Vision successfully pivoted from a H1-heavy seasonal model to an all-weather performer, delivering 28% Q4 revenue growth despite a weak summer, driven by strategic inventory stocking ahead of OEM price hikes and accelerated expansion in Uttar Pradesh. The shift in product mix toward higher-ASP but lower-margin mobiles/laptops compressed reported margins, masking the underlying operating leverage maturing stores will provide in FY27.
